items.description: VN 'co' (have/exist) calques existential clauses to 'have': '[place] have [NP]'. English uses 'there is/are [NP] [place]'.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on a locative-fronted clause ([in/at/on/here/there] ...) whose verb is 'have/has' with NO animate possessor subject, then a noun phrase. Rewrite to 'There is/are <NP> <locative>' (number-agree is/are with the NP). Do NOT fire on possessive 'have' with a personal subject ('I/we/she have ...').
items.fp_risk_note: High. 'have' is overwhelmingly correct possession ('I have a car', 'We have a meeting'). Restrict strictly to the subjectless/locative-fronted existential frame; never rewrite a clause whose subject is a person/pronoun possessor.

positive.input: In my city have many parks.
positive.expectedCorrection: There are many parks in my city.

liveEngine.corrected: In my city have many parks.

positive.notes: GAP: plural NP -> 'there are'. Engine abstains today.

positive.input: In the box have a book.
positive.expectedCorrection: There is a book in the box.

liveEngine.corrected: In the box have a book.

positive.notes: GAP: singular NP -> 'there is'. Engine abstains today.

negative.notes: Confusable: possessive 'have' with a personal subject — must not become 'there is'; live-engine verified abstains.

negative.input: There are many parks in my city.
negative.expectedCorrection: There are many parks in my city.

liveEngine.corrected: There are many parks in my city.

negative.notes: Already-correct target form; live-engine verified abstains.

items.description: VN is pro-drop and has no dummy subject, so ambient/weather predicates surface subjectless: '[time/place] very <adj>'. English requires the expletive 'it': 'It is very <adj> ...'.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on a subjectless ambient predicate (optional time/place adjunct + 'very'/adjective, no subject NP, no verb). Insert 'It is' and reorder the adjunct: 'It is very <adj> <adjunct>'. Do NOT fire when a subject is already present ('I am cold', 'The weather is hot').
items.fp_risk_note: Medium-high. Must not touch clauses that already have a subject ('I am cold', 'The weather is hot today'). Anchor on the genuinely subjectless ambient fragment; do not insert 'it' in front of an existing subject.

positive.expectedCorrection: It is very cold in winter.
It is very windy outside now.

negative.notes: Already-correct target form; live-engine verified abstains.
Confusable: an explicit subject is present — must not prepend 'it'; live-engine verified abstains.
Confusable: personal-subject experience ('I am cold' != weather 'it is cold'); live-engine verified abstains.

items.description: VN places attributive adjectives AFTER the noun ('cho den' = dog black), so learners produce '[det] [noun] [adj]'. English is prenominal: '[det] [adj] [noun]'.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on [determiner + common-noun + attributive-adjective] at a noun-phrase boundary; swap to [determiner + adjective + noun]. Do NOT fire on postnominal adjectives that are correct: indefinite pronouns ('something new', 'anything wrong') and fixed phrases ('attorney general').
items.fp_risk_note: Medium-high. Postnominal adjectives ARE correct after indefinite pronouns ('something/anything/nothing + adj') and in lexicalized phrases. Gate on a [det + common-noun + adj] frame; never reorder 'something new'.

negative.notes: Already-correct prenominal order; live-engine verified abstains.
Confusable: postnominal adjective is REQUIRED after an indefinite pronoun — must not reorder; live-engine verified abstains.

items.description: VN forms comparatives analytically ('hon' = more), so learners say 'more <short adj>' instead of the synthetic '-er': 'more tall' -> 'taller'.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on 'more' + monosyllabic (or -y bisyllabic) gradable adjective + 'than'; rewrite to the synthetic '<adj>+er'. Whitelist short adjectives (tall, young, old, big, small, easy, fast, cheap, ...). Do NOT fire on 2+ syllable adjectives that REQUIRE 'more' (beautiful, difficult, interesting, expensive).
items.fp_risk_note: High. 'more' is CORRECT for most multi-syllable adjectives ('more beautiful', 'more difficult', 'more expensive'). Only the short-adjective set takes '-er'; gate on a syllable/whitelist check or the rule will mangle correct long-adjective comparatives.

positive.input: She is more tall than me.

liveEngine.corrected: She is more tall than me.
